newsitem.title: UK: Report UK Labour MP faces suspension "speculation".
newsitem.headline: Report UK Labour MP faces suspension "speculation".

text.p: Britain's governing Labour Party on Tuesday described as speculation a newspaper report that it was about to suspend an MP from its parliamentary party following an investigation into the suicide of another of its legislators.
The Guardian newspaper said Tommy Graham, MP for the Scottish constituency of Renfrewshire West, would be suspended within the next 24 hours.
But a party spokeswoman said: "All the reports so far are speculation. We will keep you informed if that changes."

Labour's chief whip Nick Brown, who is responsible for party discipline in parliament, has been conducting an investigation into the death of another Scottish MP, Gordon McMaster, the member for Paisley South, in July.
In his suicide note, the 37-year-old MP is thought to have been harshly critical of Graham and the party's former deputy chief whip Lord Don Dixon.
The Guardian said Graham's suspension would be a temporary measure pending the outcome of a full investigation into the Paisley Labour Party by the party's national executive.
The controversy over McMaster's death comes as an unwelcome distraction to Labour ahead of the September 11 referendum on its plan for a Scottish parliament.
Scottish Secretary Donald Dewar is due later on Tuesday to launch the "yes" campaign in the referendum along with representatives of the Liberal Democrat and Scottish National Parties.
Already one Scottish Labour MP has been suspended from the parliamentary party.
The party took action against Mohammed Sarwar, Britain's first Muslim MP, who represents the Govan division of Glasgow, after an investigation into bribery allegations.
